thread:
nova: Small question from canary today: observed perf cliffs when switching from int8->4bit at batch sizes 1->4. Is that expected?

rahul: Unfortunately yes sometimes due to packing kernels and memory alignment. 4-bit kernels prefer packed batch sizes (e.g., multiples of 8) otherwise overhead for bit manipulation rises.

mina: For user-facing SLOs should we restrict allowed batch sizes when pinned to 4bit, or have runtime do internal batch padding?

nova: Padding adds token-level latency variability. Ops suggested: only allow 4bit on endpoints with p95 latency headroom > 20%.

rahul: Another mitigation: have a quick path that detects small-batch and falls back to int8 for those requests. That requires per-request decisioning latency ~200us.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary note: we have 8 endpoints with 4bit allowed. Monitor p95 for all.

mina: Action: document kernel constraints for 4bit in the profile so ops can set sensible defaults. Also add runtime flag to auto-fallback small-batch.

nova: OK will add to the playbook.
